qt: to the Commission Katri Kulmuni (Renew), Merja Kyllönen (The Left) Subject:
National individual approval of N2 diesel pickup trucks under Regulation (EU)

Since summer 2024, the Finnish approval authority (Traficom) has required compliance with the G11 rules on auxiliary emission control strategies to be demonstrated by means of an EU type-approval certificate for the national individual approval of N2 vehicles. As only manufacturers can obtain such certificates, US-market diesel pickups can effectively no longer be registered as light commercial vehicles (N2) in Finland. The same vehicles can still be registered as passenger cars (M1), but at substantially higher tax rates. According to importers, comparable vehicles have been approved as N2 vehicles in some other Member States. The issue concerns the means of demonstrating compliance, not lowering emission standards. 1.

Does the Commission consider this requirement compatible with Regulation (EU) 2018/8581, particularly its provisions on national individual approval, alternative requirements and the principle of proportionality?
Under Article 45 of the Regulation, can a Member State refuse to recognise another Member State’s national individual approval for such a vehicle, and under what circumstances?
Does the Commission intend to examine differences in national approval practices and promote a more harmonised approach to approving these work vehicles?

Regulation (EU) 2018/858 of 30 May 2018 on the approval and market surveillance of motor vehicles and their trailers, and of systems, components and separate technical units intended for such vehicles (ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2018/858/oj). 1
